description: PILLI SPACE LAB is a Kénitra-based team exploring space science through software, AI and data analysis. For Flame in Freefall, we aim to build an interactive dashboard that organizes NASA microgravity-combustion data, compares experiments, highlights patterns and anomalies, and explains findings with transparent, evidence-linked AI summaries. We combine Python, machine learning, web development, scientific curiosity and clear storytelling to support research into fire behaviour in space.
summary: Lunar Landing Site Navigator is a scientific decision-support prototype designed to support the preliminary assessment of potential landing sites near the Moon's South Pole, focusing on the Shackleton Crater region. Using high-resolution NASA Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) topographic datasets, the project explores terrain elevation, slope, measurement coverage, and data uncertainty. It combines Python-based geospatial processing with a React and TypeScript web interface to make lunar terrain information easier to explore and understand. The platform emphasizes scientific transparency through data provenance, methodology explanations, and clear limitations. Its goal is to help users investigate terrain characteristics and support better-informed preliminary assessments of potential lunar landing areas. It is an experimental research and visualization tool, not a certified landing-safety system.
details:
Project Overview

Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an experimental scientific decision-support platform focused on the preliminary exploration of potential lunar landing areas near the Moon's South Pole, with a focus on Shackleton Crater.

How It Works

The project uses high-resolution NASA Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) datasets, including:

  • Digital Elevation Model (DEM)
  • Slope maps
  • Total elevation uncertainty
  • Slope uncertainty
  • LOLA measurement-count maps (LDEC)

Python-based geospatial workflows process and visualize these datasets. The React and TypeScript frontend provides a mission overview, terrain-related visual material, data provenance information, methodology explanations, and scientific limitations.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The platform aims to make lunar terrain information more accessible and understandable. It supports preliminary terrain exploration and encourages transparent interpretation of elevation, slope, measurement coverage, and uncertainty.

Technologies Used

  • Python
  • NumPy
  • Rasterio
  • React
  • TypeScript
  • Vite
  • GeoTIFF geospatial datasets

Creativity and Scientific Approach

The project combines scientific geospatial processing with an interactive mission-oriented interface. It emphasizes the distinction between measured, calculated, interpolated, simulated, and demonstration data.

Limitations

This is an experimental decision-support prototype, not a certified landing-safety system. Full live integration between the scientific backend and frontend is still under development. Results must be interpreted considering data coverage, interpolation, and uncertainty.
